questions.q: What does "it works on my machine" describe?
options: A bug that only affects laptops, never servers
A mismatch between a developer's environment and test or production environments that causes an app to behave differently
A Docker command for checking compatibility
A type of container image signed by the developer
questions.explain: The phrase describes the common problem where an app runs fine in one environment but breaks in another because of differences in installed runtimes, libraries, or OS patches.

questions.q: What does a container image actually package together?
options: Only the application's compiled binary
A full copy of a guest operating system, including its own kernel
The application's code, runtime, libraries, and configuration, bundled as one unit
Just a list of commands to install dependencies at startup
questions.explain: A container image bundles the application together with its runtime, libraries, and configuration so the exact same package runs identically everywhere.

questions.q: Why do containers stay lightweight compared to running a separate virtual machine for each application?
options: Containers don't actually isolate applications from each other
Containers share the host machine's OS kernel instead of each one booting its own operating system
Containers only run one process total across the whole host
Containers compress the application code before running it
questions.explain: Containers get isolation without duplication: they share the host's kernel rather than each booting a full guest operating system, which is why they're far lighter than VMs.

questions.q: At Northbridge Retail, why does running the product-catalog and checkout services in separate containers avoid dependency conflicts?
options: Because containers automatically rewrite code to be compatible
Because each service's dependencies are isolated inside its own container and never touch the other service's dependencies
Because only one of the two services can run at a time
Because containers don't allow applications to have any dependencies
questions.explain: Each container keeps its own dependency tree walled off, so the Node.js catalog service and the Python checkout service can run on the same host without their libraries conflicting.

questions.q: Which statement best captures why container images are considered consistent across environments?
options: The same image, built once, runs as the exact same bits on a laptop, in CI, and in production
Each environment rebuilds the image from scratch using locally installed tools
Images are automatically upgraded to match whatever server they're deployed to
Consistency only applies if all environments run the same hardware
questions.explain: A container image is built once and run unchanged everywhere, which is exactly what eliminates the "it works on my machine" problem.
